I am 34 years old and have been farming our family's land in Quzhou County since I finished primary school. We have about 10 mu of flat, good-quality land here on the North China Plain. Every year I follow the wheat-maize double-cropping rotation that my father taught me, because it is the safest and most reliable system — everyone in our village does it, and the machinery, seed dealers, and grain buyers are all set up for it. I thought about planting a couple of mu of cotton for extra cash, but cotton needs too many pesticide sprays and too much hand-picking labor. With just my wife and me working the land, and both of us also needing to look after our child and my aging parents, I would rather focus on what I know best. The winter wheat is already in the ground from last October; I rotary-tilled before sowing and used bought improved seeds at about 35 jin per mu. I apply urea and compound fertilizer — roughly 24 kg of nitrogen per mu in total, with most of the phosphorus and potassium coming from the basal compound. The wheat needs four irrigations from our well, especially at jointing and heading, and I spray four times: twice for insects, once for weeds, and once for fungus when the weather turns humid. After harvest in early June, I will immediately plant summer maize directly into the wheat stubble without tilling again, using hybrid Denghai seeds, about one package per mu. Maize needs less fertilizer than wheat because the wheat straw adds something back; I put down about 11 kg nitrogen per mu in compound fertilizer at planting. Two irrigations are enough for maize here, and I spray twice for insects and weeds. If the weather cooperates, I expect about 550 kg per mu from both crops.
